authority: Owner ruling 2026-08-11 - rebind chain authorized with a stop gate: publish, verify independently, and only then renew P5. Follow-up ruling: use the OCI index path; do NOT amend WP-B to accept a single-platform manifest.
boundary: Publication and verification only. No control rebound, no credential released, no partition opened. validation_authorization remains false at _rev 0; OOS remains under DENY; WP-F remains NOT AUTHORIZED; P10 remains UNSATISFIED; the validation reader remains unassumable.

governed_identity.tag_is_not_identity: runtime-index-v1 is a convenience tag and is explicitly NON-AUTHORITATIVE. The immutable index digest is the binding.
governed_identity.why_the_index_and_not_the_child: The WP-B resolver requests ONLY index media types and parses index['manifests']. It is the preregistered 'resolve by index digest' contract. The child manifest digest is reachable THROUGH the index and is not itself an identity WP-B may bind.

publication.publisher_separation: Publication used a DEDICATED publisher identity on an ephemeral instance, never the qualification host. Simulation confirms the qualification role is explicitDeny on ecr:PutImage and the publisher role is explicitDeny on the sealed store and on assuming mr002-validation-reader. Both publisher instances were terminated after use.

publication_invariant.requirement: index.manifests must contain exactly the intended supported platform entries, with no attestation/provenance child treated as an executable platform image.
publication_invariant.why_manifest_count_is_1_and_not_2: The historical index sha256:60b15568 had manifest_count 2, but those were NOT two platforms: sha256:a4e3ac54 is the linux/amd64 image and sha256:b81cd073 is a buildx ATTESTATION manifest with platform unknown/unknown, annotated vnd.docker.reference.type=attestation-manifest. Reproducing '2' would have added a provenance child that is not an executable platform image. The new index deliberately carries exactly one platform entry.

status: PUBLISHED AND INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED - ELIGIBLE FOR P5/WP-B BINDING; NOT YET BOUND

superseded_not_bound.disposition: PRESERVED, NOT DELETED OR HIDDEN. It is part of the publication history. The publisher role denies ecr:BatchDeleteImage, so no identity in this chain can remove it.
superseded_not_bound.origin: A publication-shape mistake: plain docker push emits a single manifest, whereas the historical artifact was produced by buildx, which wraps the image in an index.
superseded_not_bound.what_it_is: A valid published single-platform artifact carrying the same verified payload lineage - its config digest IS the verified candidate.
superseded_not_bound.why_not_bound: Its media type is application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json with no manifests[] array, so the governed WP-B resolver would refuse it with malformed_index. It is incompatible with the resolver contract and was never accepted as P5/WP-B runtime identity.

transfer_provenance.identity_asserted_before_push: The publisher recomputed the archive digest, matched it, ran docker load, and asserted the loaded image ID equalled the verified candidate BEFORE any push. A mismatch would have refused.
transfer_provenance.mechanism: A narrow boundary amendment granted the qualification role s3:PutObject ONLY on s3://workbench-backups-219024422756/mr002/publish-staging/* - write-only, no read, no delete, no ECR push, no change to sealed-store or reader denials.
transfer_provenance.problem: The verified image was 438 MB on the qualification host, which correctly cannot publish.
transfer_provenance.write_only_demonstrated: The qualification host received HTTP 403 Forbidden attempting to read back its own upload. The boundary was proven, not merely configured.
